clue.text: By start of March, engaging in obligations

indicators.note: to engage in something is to be held within it, so one piece sits inside the other
'start of' keeps only the first letter of 'March'

blocks.note: ties are bonds or obligations
the opening letter of March

explanation.surface: Someone's commitments must be under way by the beginning of March.
explanation.walkthrough: M goes inside TIES to make TIMES. 'By' looks like a preposition of time, but it is the multiplication sign read aloud: three by four.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic, 'three by four' and 'three times four' are interchangeable ways of saying multiplied.

clue.text: Cover for mattress inappropriate leading to reprimand

blocks.note: ticking is the strong cotton fabric used to cover mattresses
off, as in a remark that is a bit off

explanation.surface: An unsuitable mattress cover gets someone told off.
explanation.definitionFit: A ticking-off is a scolding, an informal word for a rebuke.

clue.text: Aware military will secure new fund

indicators.note: something new is remade, so these letters are rearranged
securing something holds it fast within, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: MIL is the abbreviation for military
the letters of fund rearranged

explanation.surface: An alert army will lock in fresh funding.
explanation.definitionFit: Mindful means conscious of, alert to, aware.

clue.text: Completely full one day at the weekend — it's for all the family

blocks.note: SAT is short for Saturday
a U-rated film in Britain is a universal certificate, suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: A packed weekend day out that suits the whole family.
explanation.walkthrough: In the UK a film certified U (universal) is fine for all ages, so 'for all the family' is U-rated.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturated means soaked or filled to capacity, holding as much as possible.

clue.text: Testy brilliance ousting gloomy state after setback

indicators.note: to oust is to throw out, so one word's letters are removed from another
a setback here is a setting backwards, so the word for state runs right to left

blocks.note: splendour is magnificent brilliance
dour means stern and gloomy
to cite is to state or quote

explanation.surface: An irritable person's brilliance gives way to gloom after a reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' is the verb, not a condition, despite 'gloomy state' reading as one phrase; 'gloomy' is the word ousted.
explanation.definitionFit: Splenetic comes from the spleen, once thought the seat of bad temper, so it means irritable and peevish.

clue.text: Moves gracefully before the audience — grand final performance

blocks.note: to swan is to move in a graceful or showy way
a performer who is on is in front of the audience
G is the abbreviation for grand

explanation.surface: A star glides before the audience for a grand farewell show.
explanation.definitionFit: A swan song is a last performance, from the legend that swans sing just before dying.

clue.text: Single lecturer abandoning English university

indicators.note: abandoning something leaves it behind, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: lone means single, solitary
E is the abbreviation for English
a don is a university lecturer

explanation.surface: An unmarried tutor leaves an English university.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the University of London, not the city, which the surface hides by tucking it at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: London is a university, the federal University of London, as well as the city.

clue.text: Slight upset about Government late in the day

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads bottom to top
about means surrounding, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: a slight build is a thin one
G is the abbreviation for government

explanation.surface: A minor government crisis breaks late in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as an adverb phrase but stands for the noun, as in 'late in the day' meaning the night hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the end portion of a day, the time after dark.

clue.text: It shows what you can expect from an American caravan

definitions.text: It shows what you can expect

blocks.clueFragment: It shows what you can expect
blocks.note: first meaning: a film preview of coming attractions
second meaning: the US word for what Britons call a caravan, a towed mobile home

explanation.surface: Hints about what a holiday in a US camper van will be like.
explanation.definitionFit: A preview of a film is shown in advance; in American usage a towed living van is called by the same word.

clue.text: Item of Batman's outfit Crusader's first to take off

indicators.note: first picks only the opening letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: the initial letter of Crusader
to ape or take off someone is to mimic them

explanation.surface: The Caped Crusader is first to remove part of his costume.
explanation.walkthrough: Batman's nickname, the Caped Crusader, supplies the C. 'Take off' suggests undressing but means imitate.
explanation.definitionFit: Batman wears a long black cape, the sleeveless cloak behind his nickname.

clue.text: Force prisoners to drill?

blocks.note: cons are convicts
to drill troops is to train them

explanation.surface: Should inmates be made to do military drill?
explanation.definitionFit: To constrain someone is to compel or force them to act.

clue.text: Fruit supplied with good understanding

blocks.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good
rasp is a British informal shortening of raspberry

explanation.surface: Fruit offered alongside sound comprehension, an odd pairing.
explanation.walkthrough: The fruit comes first in the clue but second in the answer, since it is 'supplied with' the G.
explanation.definitionFit: A grasp of a subject is a firm comprehension of it.

clue.text: Conclude subordinate has dismissed one group of soldiers

indicators.note: dismissing someone sends them away, so letters leave the longer word

blocks.note: an inferior is a subordinate
the Roman numeral for one
OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A junior officer concludes after sending away a body of troops.
explanation.walkthrough: INFERIOR loses I and OR, leaving INFER. OR (other ranks) is the crossword convention for ordinary soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer is to reach a conclusion by reasoning from evidence.

clue.text: Work discussion to follow around spring

indicators.note: around means the first piece is wrapped about the second, enclosing it

blocks.note: to stalk is to follow stealthily
a hop is a little spring or jump

explanation.surface: Office chat about the season of spring that you are asked to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' tempts as the season, but it is a jump.
explanation.definitionFit: Shop talk is conversation about one's job, especially among colleagues outside working hours.

clue.text: Little support over water entering US city repeatedly

indicators.note: entering means going in, so one piece slips between others

blocks.note: a tee is a golf ball's support
NY is New York
wee is a childish word for urine
the city once again

explanation.surface: A small prop above water that keeps flowing into an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the support on top; 'repeatedly' means the city is used twice, with the water between.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeny-weeny is a childish reduplication meaning tiny.

clue.text: Expression of surprise about ancient language having word for 'glue'

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the exclamation wraps round the language

blocks.note: gee is an exclamation of surprise
Latin, the language of ancient Rome

explanation.surface: Surprise that the old Romans had a word for glue.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes the quoted word sound like a Latin translation question, but it is simply the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelatine, made by boiling animal tissue, is sticky and has long been used as an adhesive.

clue.text: Comic novelist invested in Wooster next

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it, so the name sits within the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A funny writer puts money into Bertie Wooster's next venture.
explanation.walkthrough: Wooster is P G Wodehouse's comic hero, which makes the surface lean toward Wodehouse, also a comic novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne wrote Tristram Shandy, a famously playful comic novel of the 18th century.

clue.text: Bar limits drunken behaviour of groups?

indicators.note: a drunken person staggers about, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A pub puts a cap on rowdy drinking by gangs.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'behaviour of groups' is a loose, playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribalism is loyalty to one's own group, and the conduct that goes with it.

clue.text: French writer having a lot of extra money to include murder victim

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the final letter is cut
including something takes it inside, so one piece enters the other

blocks.note: a raise is extra pay, the American word for a rise
Abel, killed by his brother Cain in Genesis

explanation.surface: A French author with a fortune is caught up in a killing.
explanation.walkthrough: The murder victim is the Bible's first, killed by his brother Cain; the extra money loses its last letter before taking him in.
explanation.definitionFit: François Rabelais was the 16th-century French author of Gargantua and Pantagruel.

clue.text: American comedian has a role in baseball

blocks.note: first meaning: W C ..., the US film comic
second meaning: a player who catches and returns the ball does this

explanation.surface: A US comic actor once played a part in a ball game.
explanation.definitionFit: W C Fields was a celebrated American comedian; in baseball the defending side fields the ball.

clue.text: Preferred artist in Strauss opera

blocks.note: elect means chosen, preferred
RA, Royal Academician, is a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A favoured performer appears in a Strauss opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Elektra (1909) is Richard Strauss's one-act opera on the Greek tragedy, here in its English spelling.

clue.text: New Zealand city's first to hear a poet from England

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the next word

blocks.note: the initial letter of hear
taken as written
John Milton, the English poet of Paradise Lost

explanation.surface: In a New Zealand city, the first chance to hear an English poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamilton is a large city on the Waikato River in New Zealand's North Island.

clue.text: Slip over area in metal country

indicators.note: in places the earlier pieces within the metal word

blocks.note: to err is to slip up
A is the abbreviation for area
tin, the metal

explanation.surface: Someone loses footing in a mining region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' means land or landscape, as in hill country, not a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is a stretch of land considered for its physical features, as in rough country.

clue.text: Pampers sailor that is aboard British ship at first

indicators.note: aboard means on a ship, carried inside it
at first keeps only the opening letter

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
AB, able seaman
i.e., Latin id est, that is
the first letter of ship

explanation.surface: Pampers nappies for a sailor's family aboard a British vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: Pampers is a brand of nappies, but here it is a verb: to coddle.
explanation.definitionFit: To baby someone is to pamper them, treating them like an infant.

clue.text: Bring up supplying restriction for old airline in warm weather

indicators.note: restricting something hems it in, so the first word closes round the second

blocks.note: to heave is to retch, to bring up food
TWA, Trans World Airlines, ceased flying in 2001

explanation.surface: Passengers on a defunct airline feel sick during a hot spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring up' suggests raising a subject, but here it means vomiting.
explanation.definitionFit: A heatwave is a spell of unusually hot weather.

clue.text: Wet weather dogging opening of Test series

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
dogging someone is following close behind, so the weather piece comes after

blocks.note: the initial letter of Test
rain is wet weather

explanation.surface: Rain hangs over the start of a Test cricket series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dogging' means following, so the rain comes after the T. A Test is an international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: A train is a series or succession, as in a train of thought or of events.

clue.text: Missile carrier having launched first

indicators.note: launching the first sends the leading letter off, removing it

blocks.note: a barrow is a cart for carrying loads

explanation.surface: A missile carrier fires its first weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: BARROW loses its B. 'Launched' fits the military surface but means only dropping a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrow is a projectile shot from a bow, an early missile.

clue.text: Not modern, out of time, coming up dull

indicators.note: out of means without, so the time letter is removed
in a down clue, coming up means rising, so the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: dated means old-fashioned
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Something old-fashioned and behind the times seems dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead can mean flat and lifeless, as in a dead colour or a dead sound.

clue.text: Additional skill and energy reflected receiving kiss

indicators.note: a reflection shows things mirrored, so the letters run backwards
receiving means taking something in, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: art is skill
E is the symbol for energy
X is the kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Extra talent and vigour show when someone receives a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means more than usual, additional.

clue.text: Spiritless, empty, with just one rug inside

indicators.note: inside places the pieces just before it within the word for empty

blocks.note: inane means empty, vacuous
the Roman numeral for one
a mat is a small rug

explanation.surface: A bare room with only a single rug feels lifeless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' looks like part of the definition beside 'Spiritless', but it is the word that wraps round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Inanimate means without life or spirit, so spiritless in the literal sense.

clue.text: Determination is evident in assistance for ballad making a comeback

indicators.note: coming back means going the other way, so these words are read right to left

blocks.note: aid is assistance
a ballad is a song
taken as written

explanation.surface: Resolve shows in helping a singer revive an old ballad.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the whole answer backwards and you get SI SONG AID: IS, then the ballad, then the assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagnosis is a doctor's determination of what illness a patient has.

clue.text: The writer's holding a lolly

indicators.note: holding something means having it inside, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: the setter's possessive: my
a means one

explanation.surface: I am holding a lollipop.
explanation.walkthrough: Lolly is British slang for money as well as a sweet on a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Lolly is informal British slang for cash, so it stands for money.
